09:05 Local Time, 07:05 GMT, 12:35 IST: When two quality sides meet, magic often follows on the cricket field. From the spectacular 434-run chase at Johannesburg in 2006 to the unforgettable 1999 World Cup semi-final, Australia and South Africa have produced some of ODI cricket’s most iconic moments. Whenever these two teams meet, we can expect quality cricket, because Australia and South Africa have a history of turning ODI cricket into theatre. Hello and welcome! It’s time for another one of those special episodes, hopefully..

The first ODI was defined by South Africa’s recovery from 29 for 2, with Matthew Breetzke’s rollicking knock of 112 from 106 balls and Marco Jansen’s 75 from 59 helping them reach 297 for 8. Their 107-run sixth-wicket stand turned the innings around, before Keshav Maharaj’s 4 for 20 helped them defend the total. Australia made a strong start to the chase, with Mitchell Marsh’s 60 from 36 and Travis Head’s 36 putting on 90 for the first wicket, while Matt Renshaw added 44 and Cooper Connolly 38. But from 129 for 1, Australia lost nine wickets for 101 runs and were bundled out for 230 in 41.2 overs.

Australia now need to win at the Wanderers to keep the series alive, while another South Africa victory would seal the series in their favour. The Aussies will have to do so without Josh Inglis, who has been ruled out after fracturing his right index finger in the previous match, with Alex Carey expected to take over the keeping duties. Aiden Markram, who missed the opening game for personal reasons, is available for the remaining ODIs, potentially strengthening South Africa’s batting. At the Wanderers, Australia will be looking to convert another promising start into a complete performance, while South Africa will hope their combination of batting resilience and spin control can put them within reach of a series-clinching win.
